title: Deterministic observed plus generated population core

scope.subject: Extend the existing seeded Personal Universe generation layer with one versioned population metadata contract, observed/generated provenance, world capability, bounded lazy system materialization, catalog indexing, and deterministic invariants without adding a second generator or database

research_summary: Personal Universe already has the right reusable foundation: a Helios-derived deterministic SeededRng/system generator, an authoritative NASA Exoplanet Archive snapshot adapter, and the pinned MIT YEIS native astronomy identity boundary. The missing product layer is not another astrophysics engine or rendering framework; it is stable versioned population metadata and bounded materialization around those existing primitives. Reuse current generators and observed catalog, make provenance/capability/version explicit, index observed lookup once, cache only focused systems with a fixed bound, and preserve canonical marker/system/planet IDs rather than adding a parallel namespace.

sources.finding: The already-adopted ISC Helios generator supplies the seeded RNG and composable star/planet/moon generation pattern used by the current Personal Universe implementation; extending that deterministic decomposition is lower risk than replacing it.

NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP/pscomppars is the project's existing authoritative source for confirmed exoplanet host and planetary parameters. Observed values remain authoritative while missing properties are represented as explicit inferred metadata.

The verified MIT YEIS commit is the fixed native astronomy identity/reference-frame boundary. Population metadata adapts to that identity instead of copying current AGPL upstream code or creating a second native universe model.

React Three Fiber is the adopted render lifecycle host, but its scene/frame abstractions do not provide deterministic astronomy population schemas, provenance, catalog indexing, or lazy system materialization; population remains data-layer logic outside the render framework.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain pinned YEIS as the native astronomy identity and hierarchy boundary; do not replace the product with a second universe engine.
The adopted R3F framework owns rendering lifecycle, not population provenance, deterministic catalog generation, indexing, or materialization; no additional framework is justified.
Reuse the existing Helios-derived deterministic generator for generated structure and the existing NASA snapshot adapter for observed facts, then add only project-specific metadata/index/cache glue.
The existing SeededRng/hash helpers and built-in Map are sufficient; another PRNG, cache package, schema runtime, or spatial database would add no value to this bounded core.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS native astronomy identity boundary
candidates.source: Verified pinned MIT YEIS commit already integrated in Personal Universe
candidates.license: MIT source at e520568; bundled catalog assets retain their own notices
candidates.reason: Keeps generated and observed population aligned with the native star/system identity already used by navigation and rendering instead of creating a second universe hierarchy.

candidates.name: Existing Helios-derived SeededRng and system generator
candidates.license: ISC upstream pattern plus project code
candidates.reason: Already provides stable per-seed decomposition for stars, planets and moons; extending metadata around it preserves insertion stability and avoids a replacement generator.

candidates.name: Existing NASA Exoplanet Archive snapshot adapter
candidates.source: Current exoplanet-hosts snapshot and generation/catalog.ts adapter
candidates.license: NASA public scientific data / archive terms; attribution retained
candidates.reason: Preserves observed host and planet facts as authoritative while allowing deterministic inferred fallback fields only where the snapshot lacks values.

candidates.reason: Would duplicate seeded generation, observed catalog handling and native hierarchy already present, while increasing migration and identity risk without product-value evidence.

coverage_matrix.capability: Deterministic generated system/world composition with insertion-stable identities
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep generation keyed by canonical seed/identity and add explicit generator version metadata instead of changing the seed topology.

coverage_matrix.capability: Observed facts remain authoritative and distinguishable from inferred/generated fields
coverage_matrix.decision: Index and adapt the existing NASA snapshot; never overwrite observed fields with generated values.

coverage_matrix.capability: Canonical navigation identity remains compatible with native astronomy and deep links
coverage_matrix.decision: Attach population metadata to current marker/system/world identities and keep pinned YEIS as the native identity boundary.

coverage_matrix.capability: Bounded focused-system materialization without universe-wide eager object graphs
coverage_matrix.decision: Add a small fixed-capacity cache and prebuilt observed lookup index around current resolvers; do not introduce a database.

decision.rationale: Preserve the current generation and native identity stack, then add a narrow versioned population contract, capability/provenance derivation, indexed observed lookup and bounded lazy system cache. This covers the product requirements with less migration risk and no new runtime dependency.
decision.fallback: If future catalog scale exceeds the bounded in-memory index/cache design, measure actual lookup/materialization cost first and run a new reuse-gate unit for a spatial/index database rather than preemptively replacing the current generator.
